Django-MOJO needs a public home that explains why the framework exists and lets developers move directly into complete, usable documentation. The finished site should pair a concise marketing landing page with a fast, searchable knowledge base for both framework developers and REST/API consumers, while keeping the repository documentation as the single source of truth.

---

## Spec

Agent-facing from here down. **Kind**: feature · **Requested by**: Ian Starnes

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Create a new public site in the NativeMojo workspace, linked to the django-mojo project, with Django-MOJO-specific title, metadata, and visual identity.
- [ ] Ship a responsive marketing homepage with a concrete value proposition, install/quick-start path, capability overview, and clear routes into documentation.
- [ ] Publish the complete content of both `docs/django_developer/` and `docs/web_developer/` as a browsable knowledge base.
- [ ] Keep the repository Markdown authoritative: site content is generated or indexed from those trees rather than maintained as a second handwritten copy.
- [ ] Provide an audience switch between “Django developers” and “Web/API developers,” hierarchical navigation, stable deep links, readable code samples, and mobile-friendly article layout.
- [ ] Provide fast client-side full-text search across article titles, headings, and body text, with keyboard-accessible results and useful empty states.
- [ ] Preserve relative links and anchors across the generated documentation, including cross-track links.
- [ ] Include accessible semantics, visible focus states, reduced-motion handling, a viewport declaration, and metadata for search/social sharing.
- [ ] Verify every changed public page visually at desktop width and verify real narrow-viewport reflow without horizontal overflow.
- [ ] Record a repeatable content-generation/update path so future documentation changes can be republished without manual page editing.

### Investigation

- **What exists**: `README.md` already contains the core marketing narrative, install command, quick-start model/REST example, and feature inventory. `docs/django_developer/` contains 102 Markdown files and `docs/web_developer/` contains 70 Markdown files (about 1.9 MB total). The repository is public, and `raw.githubusercontent.com/NativeMojo/django-mojo/main/` serves the canonical Markdown with cross-origin access. The repo already has a Material-for-MkDocs configuration and GitHub Pages workflow, but `mkdocs.yml` lists only a stale subset of the corpus. The NativeMojo Maestro workspace already hosts the separate `nativemojo` company site; no Django-MOJO project-linked site exists yet. The Maestro site platform serves static HTML/CSS/JavaScript, requires a root `index.html`, allows 8 MB total, and caps each submitted file at 200 KB.
- **What changes**: Create a distinct Django-MOJO site linked to project 12; add committed site templates/assets plus a generator that scans both documentation trees into sharded navigation and full-text indexes; deploy a static docs reader that fetches canonical Markdown from the exact indexed commit, renders it locally, and rewrites internal links.
- **Constraints**: Apply rules `nativemojo-board-conventions` and `django-mojo-build-conventions`. The first site deployment is public immediately. The repository Markdown must remain canonical. No submitted site file may exceed 200 KB. The docs reader must fail clearly when GitHub is unavailable and must not turn a fetch error into blank content. Only one django-mojo build/test process may run at a time.
- **Related files**: `README.md`; `docs/README.md`; `docs/django_developer/README.md`; `docs/django_developer/**`; `docs/web_developer/README.md`; `docs/web_developer/**`; `mkdocs.yml`; `.github/workflows/docs.yml`; new `website/django_mojo/**`; new `scripts/build_django_mojo_site.py`; generated ignored `docs_site/**`.
- **Out of scope**: Custom-domain purchase or DNS changes; authenticated/private docs; an AI chat/RAG assistant; in-browser documentation editing; rewriting the documentation corpus; changing framework behavior or REST contracts; replacing the existing GitHub Pages workflow in this item.

## Plan

### Objective

Create and publicly deploy `django-mojo.sitesmojo.com` as a NativeMojo workspace site linked to the django-mojo project. The site will combine an editorial product landing page with a static documentation reader whose navigation and searchable inventory are generated from all canonical Markdown under both developer tracks.

### Implementation

1. Add `website/django_mojo/` as the committed source surface. Create `index.html`, `docs/index.html`, `404.html`, `css/site.css`, `js/site.js`, `js/docs.js`, and a vendored, license-pinned Markdown renderer under `vendor/`. Use a warm-paper/ink/signal-green editorial direction, typographic hierarchy, asymmetric technical-detail layouts, and no stock imagery or decorative SVG. The landing page will derive its claims and quick-start code from `README.md`, with primary actions for installation, Django developer docs, REST/API docs, and GitHub.
2. Add `scripts/build_django_mojo_site.py`. It will scan every `.md` file in `docs/django_developer/` and `docs/web_developer/`, derive stable document ids from repository-relative paths, extract titles/headings/plain-text excerpts and normalized searchable bodies, group navigation by audience and directory, and write a deterministic ignored bundle under `docs_site/`. It will split catalogs and search data into deterministic shards with a conservative 150 KB target, stamp every shard with the current source commit, and expose `--check` to fail on duplicate ids, missing titles, escaping paths, broken local Markdown targets/anchors, missing required entry files, inconsistent shard commits, or any output file above the platform's reported cap.
3. Implement the docs reader in `website/django_mojo/js/docs.js`. It will load the sharded catalog immediately; resolve `?doc=<track/path>` with each track README as the default; fetch the canonical Markdown from `raw.githubusercontent.com/NativeMojo/django-mojo/<manifest-commit>/docs/`; render it with the vendored parser; add deterministic heading ids; rewrite relative `.md` links and cross-track links into reader URLs while preserving fragments; turn repository-source links that leave `docs/` into pinned GitHub blob links; keep external links explicit and safe; update document title/history; and show retryable loading/error states without discarding the navigation shell.
4. Implement the knowledge-base search in the docs reader from the generated search shards. Title, heading, path, excerpt, and full-body matches will be local to the deployed site, deterministic, and available without a 172-request browser warm-up. Load only the lightweight catalog at startup and fetch the bounded sub-200-KB search shards on the first substantive query, rank results after all shards settle, report any shard failure as an incomplete index, and cache successful shards for the session. The search dialog/listbox will support `/` or Cmd/Ctrl+K, arrow keys, Enter, Escape, visible progress, useful no-results/error states, and a result cap that avoids rendering hundreds of rows.
5. Implement responsive navigation and article behavior. Desktop gets a fixed two-level documentation rail plus on-page table of contents; narrow screens get explicit menu/search controls, scroll-contained navigation, code/table overflow handling, and no horizontal page overflow. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; never hide essential content behind reveal callbacks; provide skip links, semantic landmarks, visible focus states, and copy buttons that work without blocking reading when clipboard access is unavailable.
6. Generate the bundle and validate it locally. Run the generator in build and `--check` modes; inspect its manifest counts (102 Django + 70 Web/API articles), output sizes, and link report. Exercise representative same-directory, parent-directory, cross-track, and fragment links in automated checks. Serve `docs_site/` locally and verify the homepage plus representative long, table-heavy, and code-heavy docs at desktop width; use the real browser pane at 375 px to verify reflow and `scrollWidth === clientWidth`.
7. Create the Maestro site with workspace 17, link it to project 12, use slug `django-mojo`, title `Django-MOJO`, and set a durable site brief covering positioning/source-of-truth/deployment constraints. Because the generated bundle is larger than the MCP call-safe threshold, publish it from `docs_site/` through the site's documented disk-upload API in one atomic replacement rather than emitting it through a tool argument. Inspect the public landing page and representative docs pages as real pixels. Fix the worst visual or functional issue with `update_site_files` only after re-reading the live bundle. Confirm the deployed reference scan has no missing internal assets.
8. Commit the generator, source assets, vendored license, validation coverage, and `planning/built/1216.md` with explicit pathspecs. Do not commit generated `docs_site/`, alter the framework docs themselves, update `CHANGELOG.md`, create a branch, or push.

### Design Decisions

- Use a purpose-built static reader instead of deploying the existing MkDocs output. MkDocs already provides useful fallback publication on GitHub Pages, but its stale hand-written nav omits part of the corpus and its monolithic search index is incompatible with the site's 200 KB per-file limit.
- Fetch article Markdown from the public repository at read time, pinned to the exact commit recorded by the generated catalog. This preserves one authored source of truth without allowing a mutable `main` branch to drift away from the deployed navigation; documentation updates require regenerating and atomically redeploying the site. A visible retry state is required because reading an uncached article depends on GitHub availability.
- Use stable query URLs (`/docs/?doc=django_developer/core/mojo_model#graphs`) rather than pretending the static platform can serve 172 generated route trees. This keeps deep links durable without duplicating article bodies into the deployment.
- Full-body search uses generated plain-text shards, not live article fan-out. The shards are derivative build artifacts, never hand-edited content, and remain well inside the 8 MB bundle while each keeps conservative headroom below the per-file cap.
- Keep the Django-MOJO product visual identity related to, but distinct from, the Native Mojo company site. The parent site's cube mark and company-builder positioning do not become product-page decoration or copy.

### Edge Cases and Error Handling

- Reject manifest paths that leave the two allowed docs roots; encode all reader URLs and never concatenate an untrusted query directly into the fetch origin.
- Unknown document ids fall back to a branded not-found state with links to both track roots, not the marketing homepage and not a blank article.
- Network, HTTP, and Markdown-render failures retain the shell and identify the requested source path with Retry and GitHub-source actions.
- Rewrite only repository-local Markdown targets. Preserve external, mail, and same-document fragment links; leave non-Markdown assets on their absolute raw GitHub URL.
- Generate collision-safe heading ids and resolve GitHub-style anchor links case-insensitively where practical; the checker reports unresolved local fragments before deployment.
- Treat any failed search shard as an incomplete index and say so; never present partial results as exhaustive.
- Tables and code blocks scroll inside the article. Long tokens, API paths, and nested navigation labels cannot widen the page.

### Testing and Documentation

- Add focused generator checks alongside `scripts/build_django_mojo_site.py` (or a small `tests/test_scripts/` module if the existing test harness cleanly supports it) for manifest counts, deterministic ordering, title/heading extraction, relative-link resolution, traversal rejection, duplicate ids, fragment validation, and file-size limits.
- Add browser-level smoke assertions against the generated local site for landing/docs entry points, default-track loading, known deep links, search keyboard flow, and error-state rendering. Only one browser/test runner may operate at a time.
- Treat `website/django_mojo/README.md` as the operator guide: explain the source/output split, build/check commands, public GitHub dependency, deployment file map, slug/project linkage, and the fact that deployment is immediately public.
- Record all public copy and metadata in the site brief so a later site-editing session does not reverse product positioning or duplicate the docs corpus.

### Verification

- **Tier: targeted.** The change is isolated to new site-generation/source files and does not touch Django framework runtime, models, migrations, REST contracts, or the canonical documentation body. There is no meaningful pre-edit Django-suite baseline because no existing test module covers a non-existent site surface.
- Closing verification: generator `--check`; focused generator/link tests; a deliberate rename/heading-change fixture proving catalog/content commit pinning; local HTTP/browser smoke checks; desktop screenshots read for the landing page and at least one representative page from each docs track; real 375 px browser-pane reflow with equal `scrollWidth`/`clientWidth`; live post-deploy screenshots of the landing page and both docs tracks; an exhaustive live crawl of every catalog document and every rewritten local target/fragment; Maestro reference scan with zero missing internal files.

### Challenge

| # | Objection | Disposition | Evidence / what changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|-------------------------|
| 1 | A single 172-document manifest may cross the 200 KB file cap. | **amended** | A measured compact draft was already 167,865 bytes, leaving inadequate growth room. The generator now shards catalogs/search data at a 150 KB target and checks every output against the platform cap. |
| 2 | A build-time manifest paired with read-time `main` will drift after document renames or heading changes. | **amended** | Article fetches now use the exact source commit embedded in every catalog shard, and verification includes a later-revision rename/heading fixture. |
| 3 | Fetching all 172 Markdown files to warm full-body search is neither fast nor stable. | **amended** | A six-way cold fetch took about seven seconds on the build machine. Full-body search now uses generated, local, sub-200-KB text shards; only the selected article is fetched from GitHub. |
| 4 | Representative screenshots and the static reference graph cannot prove all external article fetches and rewritten anchors. | **amended** | Closing verification now includes an exhaustive live crawl of every catalog document and every local target/fragment from the deployed origin. |
- Escalate to a whole-suite Django run only if implementation crosses into shared framework code, models, migrations, REST metadata, or three existing apps. No `--full` run is planned.
